processes.name: mDNSResponder
processes.normal: DNS answers are small, so mDNSResponder usually moves less data than the apps that it works for.
processes.reduce: Find the app that makes the lookups. Its own traffic often rises at the same time in Activity Monitor.
processes.summary: Part of macOS. It handles system DNS lookups for apps and runs Bonjour on the local network, so its traffic can include other apps' name lookups.

processes.block: Blocking it should have little effect. Photos analysis is local, and Apple does not document network use.
breaks: A firewall rule is unlikely to change anything visible.
If it does connect, some Photos search features could fail. Apple does not say which.
processes.name: mediaanalysisd
processes.normal: This daemon is busy on the CPU after you add many photos, not on the network.
processes.reduce: Let the analysis finish. Keep the Mac on power.
processes.summary: Part of macOS. It analyses media for Photos and other services. Apple does not document it, and its work is local as far as the launchd file shows.

processes.block: Blocking it stops Office and other Microsoft app updates, including security fixes. On a hotspot, pause it or update later instead.
breaks: Office, Teams and other Microsoft apps stop getting updates and security fixes.
Help › Check for Updates in Microsoft apps can't find updates.
heavy: A Mac that was off for a while
processes.name: Microsoft AutoUpdate
processes.normal: Small checks a couple of times a day are usual.
processes.reduce: Open a Microsoft app, such as Word. Choose Help › Check for Updates. The MAU window opens.
processes.summary: Microsoft's updater for Office, Teams and other Microsoft apps on the Mac. It checks for updates and, by default, downloads and installs them.

processes.block: Your organisation manages this agent. Blocking its URLs stops protection reporting and updates, and the device can show as disconnected.
breaks: The device cannot report to the Microsoft Defender portal.
Cloud-delivered protection and updates stop.
Web and network protection stops where it needs SmartScreen hosts.
A proxy that inspects TLS or needs a login breaks the connection.
processes.name: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint
processes.normal: Microsoft does not publish figures for normal traffic. Expect small, regular exchanges with Microsoft's cloud.
processes.reduce: Do not change this agent yourself. Ask your administrator if its traffic causes a problem.
processes.summary: Microsoft's endpoint security agent for Mac. It reports to Microsoft's cloud on port 443, downloads updates, and does not support authenticated proxies or SSL inspection.

processes.block: Blocking Edge stops your browsing in it. Blocking only some Microsoft endpoints turns off the matching feature.
breaks: Blocking the update service stops Edge from updating.
Blocking sign-in endpoints stops profile sign-in and sync.
Blocking SmartScreen hosts removes that protection.
Blocking Copilot's internal URLs can cause errors. Microsoft says to use policies instead.
processes.name: Microsoft Edge
processes.normal: Browsing traffic depends on the sites that you open.
processes.reduce: Use Edge's own settings to turn off features that you do not use, such as sync.
processes.summary: The Edge browser. Microsoft lists endpoints for updates, sign-in, sync, SmartScreen, passwords, translation and Copilot, in addition to your browsing.

processes.block: Blocking Outlook's endpoints stops mail and calendar sync. Block them only if you do not use Outlook on this Mac.
breaks: New mail does not arrive and sent mail does not leave.
Calendar items stop syncing.
A mail proxy that is not configured correctly stops the Exchange connection.
processes.name: Microsoft Outlook
processes.normal: Microsoft does not publish figures for idle traffic. Outlook keeps your mailbox current, so small, regular traffic is normal.
processes.reduce: Keep large attachments out of mail. Share a link instead.
processes.summary: Outlook for Mac. For Microsoft 365 mail, Microsoft lists Exchange Online endpoints on TCP 443 and 80, and IMAP, POP and SMTP ports for other clients.

processes.block: Blocking Teams stops chat, calls and meetings. Blocking UDP 3478 to 3481 makes calls fall back to TCP or fail.
breaks: You cannot sign in, chat or join meetings in the app.
Blocking UDP 3478 to 3481 degrades or breaks audio, video and sharing.
Microsoft says that other Microsoft 365 flows must stay open for Teams to work.
processes.name: Microsoft Teams
processes.normal: Small, steady HTTPS traffic while Teams is open is usual.
processes.reduce: Turn off your camera when you do not need it. Video uses most of the data.
processes.summary: The Microsoft Teams app. Chat and sign-in use HTTPS. Calls and meetings send audio, video and screen sharing, preferably over UDP.

processes.block: Blocking it stops downloads of models, voices and other assets that macOS features need. To stop the biggest download, turn off Apple Intelligence.
breaks: Apple Intelligence can't finish setting up, and new models after an update don't arrive.
New voices, languages and dictionaries can't download.
Apple doesn't document every asset it handles, so other features that need a download may fail too.
processes.name: mobileassetd
processes.normal: Downloads after a macOS update, or after you turn on a feature, are usual. Apple Intelligence models can be several gigabytes.
processes.reduce: Do macOS updates on your usual network. The asset downloads follow them.
processes.summary: Part of macOS, not documented by Apple. Kilobat sees it download system assets such as Apple Intelligence models, voices, fonts and dictionaries.

processes.block: Blocking it stops Shared Albums and My Photo Stream from updating. Leave an album in Photos instead.
breaks: Shared Albums stop uploading and downloading.
Notifications about new shared photos may not arrive.
heavy: Adding many photos to a shared album
processes.name: mstreamd
processes.normal: Short bursts when you add to or open a shared album are normal.
processes.reduce: Open Photos. Leave shared albums that you do not follow, or stop adding to them.
processes.summary: Part of macOS. It is responsible for My Photo Stream and Shared Albums in Photos.

processes.block: Blocking Mullvad stops the tunnel. Its kill switch is always on, so the app can leave this Mac without internet while the tunnel is down.
breaks: The tunnel cannot form, so the VPN does not connect.
The kill switch blocks other traffic while the app is on and the tunnel is down.
Login and server updates that use Mullvad's API fail, unless a bridge method works.
processes.name: Mullvad VPN
processes.normal: While connected, almost all of this Mac's internet traffic goes through the tunnel. Its size is the size of what your apps send, plus overhead.
processes.reduce: If the tunnel does not connect on a network, open Settings › VPN settings › Anti-censorship. Try a WireGuard port, then LWO, QUIC, Shadowsocks and UDP-over-TCP in turn.
processes.summary: Mullvad's VPN app. It tunnels your traffic with WireGuard over UDP and can disguise it with LWO, QUIC, Shadowsocks or UDP-over-TCP on other ports.

processes.block: Don't block them. VPNs and content filters, including Kilobat's firewall, can't run without them.
breaks: VPN connections can't start, or stop carrying traffic.
Content filters, including Kilobat's network filter, stop working.
VPN and filter settings may fail to apply.
processes.name: nesessionmanager
processes.normal: With a VPN on, a lot of traffic under these processes is normal. It is your traffic, inside the tunnel.
processes.reduce: To stop a VPN, turn it off in the VPN app or in Apple menu › System Settings › VPN.
processes.summary: Part of macOS. They run Network Extension sessions, such as VPNs and content filters, and host their plug-ins, so VPN traffic can show under them.

processes.block: Safe to block if you don't share files with Windows computers. It's cleaner to turn off File Sharing, which configures it.
breaks: Windows computers may not find this Mac by its NetBIOS name.
Browsing Windows computers and workgroups from the Finder may show fewer computers.
processes.name: netbiosd
processes.normal: Small local traffic is usual. It doesn't use your internet connection.
processes.reduce: Check whether you share files. Choose Apple menu › System Settings › General › Sharing.
processes.summary: Part of macOS. It registers and browses NetBIOS names for Windows-style file sharing. Its traffic stays on the local network.

processes.block: Blocking it can break iCloud Private Relay and Apple services that use its proxy. To stop the relay, turn off Private Relay instead.
breaks: iCloud Private Relay can't connect, so Safari may fail to load pages while it is on.
Apple system services that use the proxy may fail. Apple doesn't list them.
processes.name: networkserviceproxy
processes.normal: With Private Relay off, its traffic is usually small.
processes.reduce: To turn off Private Relay, choose Apple menu › System Settings. Click your name, then iCloud, then Private Relay.
processes.summary: Part of macOS. It is the transparent proxy for Apple system services and can carry iCloud Private Relay traffic, so other apps' browsing can show under it.

processes.block: Blocking it stops the News feed and widgets from loading new stories. Nothing else in macOS depends on it.
breaks: The Today feed and widgets stop updating.
Downloaded issues and saved stories may not load.
News notifications may stop.
processes.name: newsd
processes.normal: Short bursts when you open News or the Today feed are normal.
processes.reduce: In News, review the channels and topics that you follow. Block channels or topics that you do not want, as Apple's guide describes.
processes.summary: Part of macOS. It runs Apple News feeds and downloads. Apple does not document the daemon, but the News guide describes the feed.

processes.block: Blocking the client's server stops syncing. Local files stay on the Mac, and changes wait until the server is reachable again.
breaks: Local changes cannot upload to your server.
Remote changes cannot download, and server notifications do not arrive.
Update checks fail if the update host is blocked. The manual does not name that host.
processes.name: Nextcloud
processes.normal: Which host the client talks to depends on your server. The manual does not name a Nextcloud-run host for sync.
processes.reduce: To limit the client's speed, open the Network tab in its settings and set an upload or download limit.
processes.summary: Nextcloud's sync client. It talks to the Nextcloud server that you set up, polls it every 30 seconds by default, and has its own proxy and bandwidth settings.

processes.block: Blocking node blocks every Node.js program at once. Block the specific host instead, or stop the script you don't recognise.
breaks: npm and npx can't install packages.
Dev servers, CLIs, AI agents and MCP servers that run on Node.js lose the network.
The rule applies to every program that this node binary runs.
processes.maker: OpenJS Foundation (Node.js), installed by you or a tool
processes.name: node
processes.normal: Traffic while you install packages or run a tool is normal.
processes.reduce: Find what the process runs. In Terminal, show its command line, using its process ID.
processes.summary: The Node.js runtime, not part of macOS. It connects only when a script asks, such as npm installing packages, a dev server, an AI agent or an MCP server.

processes.block: Blocking NordVPN's ports stops the tunnel from connecting. Block only the protocol that you do not use, such as OpenVPN, if you use NordLynx.
breaks: The VPN cannot connect on a protocol whose ports are blocked.
If you block UDP 51820 and use NordLynx, the tunnel fails.
Blocking TCP 443 also affects normal web traffic, so use a rule for the app instead.
processes.name: NordVPN
processes.normal: While connected, your Mac's traffic goes through the tunnel. Its size is the size of what your apps send, plus overhead.
processes.reduce: To change the protocol, click the gear icon in the app, choose General, and click the current protocol.
processes.summary: NordVPN's VPN client. Nord lists the outbound ports for each protocol, such as UDP 51820 for NordLynx and TCP 443 or UDP 1194 for OpenVPN.

processes.block: Blocking Notion's domains stops pages loading and edits saving. Notion shows offline and image errors when a network blocks it.
breaks: Pages and databases cannot load from Notion's servers.
Edits cannot save, and Notion can show "Cannot save changes" or "There was an issue persisting your edits".
Images and files that use notionusercontent.com show "Go online to view this image".
API integrations that use api.notion.com fail.
processes.name: Notion
processes.normal: Notion's pages do not give a normal data volume. Traffic follows what you open and edit, so a busy workspace sends more than an idle one.
processes.reduce: To check that your network allows Notion, open the app on another network and compare. VPNs are the most common cause of image errors.
processes.summary: Notion's desktop app. Notion publishes the domains and IP ranges that it needs, led by notion.com, and tells network admins to allowlist them.

processes.block: Blocking it stops the background downloads and uploads of every app that hands transfers to macOS. Pause the one app instead.
breaks: Background downloads in apps that use it, such as podcast episodes and media for offline use, wait or fail.
Background uploads from those apps wait or fail.
Each app decides what to show when the transfer fails, so the error may not name the network.
processes.name: nsurlsessiond
processes.normal: Some nsurlsessiond traffic is a normal part of macOS. The amount depends only on what your apps asked for. With no pending transfers, it is quiet.
processes.reduce: Find the app that asked for the download. Think about what you started just before, for example a podcast subscription.
processes.summary: Part of macOS. It does background downloads and uploads that apps hand to macOS, so its traffic belongs to those apps.

processes.block: Obsidian works offline. Blocking its hosts only stops Sync, Publish, licence checks and updates. Notes in a local vault stay available.
breaks: Obsidian Sync stops, and changes stop copying between your devices.
Obsidian Publish cannot update your public site.
Account and licence actions in Settings that call api.obsidian.md fail.
Early access updates from releases.obsidian.md and release checks on GitHub fail.
Plugins that need the internet stop working.
processes.name: Obsidian
processes.normal: Standard procedures for securing applications apply if you use no Sync, Publish, plugins or themes. The app is built to work offline.
processes.reduce: To see which Sync server your vault uses, open Settings › Sync and click Copy Debug Info. Look for the Host server line.
processes.summary: Obsidian is an offline notes app. Its own help lists the connections that it makes, all on HTTPS port 443, for Sync, Publish, licences, updates and GitHub checks.

processes.block: Blocking Ollama's outbound traffic stops model pulls and cloud features. Local models that you already have keep working.
breaks: ollama pull and model updates fail.
Cloud models and web search stop.
Blocking port 11434 on the loopback address breaks every app that talks to your local Ollama.
processes.name: ollama
processes.normal: Outside a download, a local-only Ollama sends nothing to the internet that the FAQ describes.
processes.reduce: To keep Ollama local, leave OLLAMA_HOST unset. It then binds to 127.0.0.1.
processes.summary: Ollama runs language models locally. It listens on 127.0.0.1 port 11434 by default and downloads models from the internet when you pull them.

processes.block: Blocking it stops OneDrive sync on this Mac. Your local files stay, but changes don't reach the cloud. Pause it or cap its rate instead.
breaks: Files don't upload or download, so this Mac and your other devices drift apart.
Office files saved to OneDrive don't reach your other devices.
Sign-in to OneDrive may fail if its sign-in hosts are blocked too.
processes.name: OneDrive
processes.normal: Bursts after you change files are usual. The amount is about the size of the files.
processes.reduce: Control-click the OneDrive icon in the menu bar. Choose to pause for 2, 8 or 24 hours. Sync resumes on its own after that.
processes.summary: Microsoft's OneDrive sync app. It uploads and downloads your OneDrive files. It pauses on metered networks on its own.

processes.block: Blocking Parallels' hosts breaks activation and licence checks. Blocking the app's traffic can also cut off virtual machines that use the Mac's connection.
breaks: Licence validation and activation can fail with an error such as "Unable to perform the operation".
Account management and feedback to Parallels fail.
Virtual machines in Shared mode lose their internet access if their traffic is blocked.
heavy: Windows Update inside a virtual machine
Bridged mode on a shared network
processes.name: Parallels Desktop
processes.normal: The traffic to Parallels' own hosts is small and uses port 443. Parallels does not state how often the app contacts them.
processes.reduce: If activation fails, check that this Mac is online and not behind a proxy. Parallels lists a blocked firewall and a proxy as causes.
processes.summary: Parallels runs virtual machines. Parallels documents seven hosts that it contacts on port 443, and three networking modes that decide how your virtual machines reach the network.

processes.block: Safe to block if you don't want web suggestions. Local Spotlight search keeps working. It's cleaner to turn suggestions off in settings.
breaks: Siri, Spotlight and Safari suggestions from the web stop appearing.
Look Up and #images can't load their content.
Apple News article search may stop working.
processes.name: parsecd
processes.normal: Small requests while you search are usual.
processes.reduce: Choose Apple menu › System Settings › Spotlight. Turn off the search results and suggestions that you don't use.
processes.summary: Part of macOS. It handles Siri, Spotlight and Safari suggestions and Look Up, so it connects to Apple while you search or type.

processes.block: Blocking them can break Apple Pay and Wallet on this Mac. Remove cards in Wallet instead.
breaks: Apple Pay payments in Safari and in apps may fail.
Wallet cannot add, update or remove cards and passes.
Passes with background updates stop updating.
heavy: Adding or removing a card or pass
processes.name: passd
processes.normal: Both daemons are idle most of the time. Short bursts when you open Wallet, add a card or pay are normal.
processes.reduce: Open Wallet and remove cards or passes that you do not use.
processes.summary: Part of macOS. passd runs Apple Pay and Wallet, and financed supports it. Apple documents the design of Apple Pay but not these daemons' network use.

processes.block: Blocking it stops leaked password warnings for saved passwords. Nothing else depends on it.
breaks: Password Monitoring cannot compare your saved passwords with the leaked list, so no warnings appear.
You may get no alert for a password that has appeared in a data leak.
heavy: A first run after you turn the feature on
processes.name: PasswordBreachAgent
processes.normal: The traffic is small and regular. Apple designs each lookup to be a short exchange of hashed prefixes and blinded values.
processes.reduce: Change any password that you get a leak warning for.
processes.summary: Part of macOS. It checks whether saved website passwords appear in a data leak. Apple says the check does not send the password.

processes.block: Blocking TCP 32400 stops other devices from reaching your library. Block Plex only if you do not want to share media.
breaks: Other Plex apps on your network cannot connect to the server.
Remote Access fails when the port is blocked or when the checks from plex.tv cannot reach the server.
Devices that use DLNA or GDM discovery stop finding the server when their ports are blocked.
processes.name: Plex Media Server
processes.normal: Plex does not publish figures for idle traffic. With no one watching, you should expect small traffic to plex.tv and on the local network.
processes.reduce: Open Settings › Server › Remote Access in the Plex Web App. Turn Remote Access off if you only use Plex at home.
processes.summary: Plex's media server for Mac. It listens on TCP port 32400 and, for Remote Access, asks the router to forward a port through UPnP or NAT-PMP.

processes.block: Blocking it stops Apple Intelligence features that need Private Cloud Compute. On-device features keep working.
breaks: Apple Intelligence requests that need a larger model fail.
Features that use Private Cloud Compute, as listed in the Apple Intelligence Report, stop working.
processes.name: privatecloudcomputed
processes.normal: When you use Apple Intelligence, some traffic is expected. Each request and answer is small next to a download.
processes.reduce: Use fewer Apple Intelligence features, or turn Apple Intelligence off in System Settings › Apple Intelligence & Siri.
processes.summary: Part of macOS. It encrypts and sends Apple Intelligence requests that need a larger model to Apple's Private Cloud Compute servers.

processes.block: Blocking it can stop encrypted key sync and backup. Some iCloud data may become unreadable on a new device.
breaks: Keys do not sync to your other devices.
iCloud features that need those keys may fail on a new device.
heavy: A new device or a change of data protection
processes.name: ProtectedCloudKeySyncing
processes.normal: Small bursts when keys change are expected.
processes.reduce: Choose Apple menu › System Settings. Click your name, then click iCloud, and review Advanced Data Protection.
processes.summary: Part of macOS. It manages backup and syncing of encrypted PCS keys to CloudKit.

processes.block: Blocking Proton's ports stops the tunnel from connecting, and Proton does not publish a port list. Block them only where you do not use Proton VPN.
breaks: The tunnel fails when the protocol and backup ports are all blocked.
A firewall rule that blocks the WireGuard network extension stops new connections.
processes.name: Proton VPN
processes.normal: Proton does not publish figures for idle traffic. While connected, the traffic that you route through the tunnel moves through the VPN server.
processes.reduce: Leave Smart Protocol on. Proton enables it by default, and it handles blocked protocols.
processes.summary: Proton's VPN app. It tunnels your traffic over a protocol that Smart Protocol picks, and falls back to other protocols and ports when a network blocks one.

processes.block: Blocking it is safe for the internet, but Handoff and other features between your Apple devices stop.
breaks: Handoff between this Mac and your other devices stops.
Phone call handoff and other Continuity features that need it may stop.
Blocking incoming connections for it in the macOS firewall has the same effect on the features that listen.
processes.name: rapportd
processes.normal: Small amounts of local traffic are usual when you have other Apple devices nearby.
processes.reduce: Choose Apple menu › System Settings › General › AirDrop & Continuity.
processes.summary: Part of macOS. It connects this Mac to your other Apple devices on the local network for Handoff, phone calls and other Continuity features.

processes.block: Blocking Raycast cuts AI providers, extension installs, sync and updates. Raycast does not publish a host list, so a block is a rule for the app.
breaks: AI chat stops when its provider cannot be reached.
Extension installs and updates, the updater and sync cannot complete.
If you block a custom provider's address, requests to that provider fail. Raycast never falls back to another provider.
processes.name: Raycast
processes.normal: Raycast's pages give no normal data volume. Traffic follows what you use, such as AI chat, extensions and sync.
processes.reduce: To send Raycast's traffic through a proxy, open Settings › Advanced and turn on Use System Proxy Settings.
processes.summary: Raycast is a launcher with AI and extensions. Its docs describe a system proxy setting, proxy variables, a custom certificate option and direct calls to custom AI providers.

processes.block: Blocking it stops Reminders from syncing and alerting. Turn off Reminders in iCloud settings instead.
breaks: Reminders stop syncing with your other devices and with shared lists.
Alerts for time-based and location-based reminders may not arrive.
Changes stay on this Mac until the daemon can connect again.
processes.name: remindd
processes.normal: Short bursts after you edit a list, or when someone changes a shared list, are normal.
processes.reduce: Choose Apple menu › System Settings. Click your name, then click iCloud, and open the list of apps that use iCloud.
processes.summary: Part of macOS. It runs Reminders data, alerts and sync. The full Reminders features need updated iCloud reminders.

processes.block: Blocking them doesn't save internet data. Xcode's wireless installs and debugging, and other paired-device features, stop.
breaks: Xcode can't find, install to or debug a device over the network.
Other features that discover paired devices may stop. Apple doesn't document them all.
heavy: Installing a build on a device
processes.name: remotepairingd
processes.normal: If you use Xcode with a device, or another feature that pairs devices, traffic to that device is expected.
processes.reduce: Connect the device with a cable when you install or debug apps.
processes.summary: Part of macOS and Xcode's device support. They find and talk to paired iPhones and iPads, mostly on the local network.

processes.block: Blocking diagnostic uploads prevents Apple from receiving reports. To stop automatic analytics uploads, turn off Share Mac Analytics instead.
breaks: Apple stops getting your diagnostic reports, which help it fix bugs.
Developers who receive reports through Apple, with Share with app developers on, stop getting yours.
processes.name: SubmitDiagInfo
processes.normal: If you share analytics, the uploads are small and periodic.
processes.reduce: Choose Apple menu › System Settings › Privacy & Security. Click Analytics & Improvements.
processes.summary: Part of macOS. ReportCrash saves crash reports on the Mac. SubmitDiagInfo sends diagnostic and usage information to Apple, but only if you opted in.

processes.block: Blocking it may stop places-based suggestions in Maps, Calendar and Reminders. Turn off Significant Locations instead.
breaks: Features that predict where you go may stop.
Cloud storage of learned places, if used, stops.
processes.name: routined
processes.normal: Network use is not documented. Expect little.
processes.reduce: Choose Apple menu › System Settings › Privacy & Security › Location Services. Scroll to System Services and click Details.
processes.summary: Part of macOS. It learns your historical location patterns. Apple says Significant Locations are encrypted and unreadable by Apple.

processes.block: Blocking it stops Safari bookmarks, Reading List and tabs from syncing. Turn Safari off in iCloud settings instead.
breaks: Safari bookmarks stop syncing with your other devices.
Reading List and tab sharing stop.
Changes stay on this Mac.
processes.name: SafariBookmarksSyncAgent
processes.normal: Short bursts when you change bookmarks are normal.
processes.reduce: Choose Apple menu › System Settings. Click your name, then click iCloud, and open the list of apps that use iCloud.
processes.summary: Part of macOS. It syncs Safari bookmarks, Reading List and tabs with iCloud through CloudKit.

processes.block: Safe to block if nobody needs to reach this Mac remotely. It's better to turn off Screen Sharing in Sharing settings.
breaks: Other computers can't view or control this Mac with Screen Sharing or a VNC app.
Apple Remote Desktop management of this Mac stops, if your organization uses it.
processes.name: screensharingd
processes.normal: With no session open, its traffic is small or none.
processes.reduce: Choose Apple menu › System Settings › General › Sharing.
processes.summary: Part of macOS. It accepts Screen Sharing and VNC connections from other computers, so another person can see and control this Mac.

processes.block: Blocking it stops Screen Time data syncing between devices. For a child's device, it can stop limits from arriving.
breaks: Screen Time reports stop including your other devices.
Changes a parent makes to a child's limits may not arrive, and the child's usage may not reach the parent.
processes.name: ScreenTimeAgent
processes.normal: Small, occasional sync traffic is usual with Screen Time on.
processes.reduce: Choose Apple menu › System Settings › Screen Time.
processes.summary: Part of macOS. It supports Screen Time, which can sync your usage and limits across your devices through iCloud.

processes.block: Don't block it. Apps that use the keychain depend on it, and iCloud Keychain sync stops.
breaks: Passwords, passkeys and Wi-Fi passwords stop syncing with your other devices.
New devices can't join your iCloud Keychain.
Apps on this Mac that read the keychain may fail if keychain access is affected.
processes.name: secd
processes.normal: Small, occasional sync traffic is usual with iCloud Keychain on. Keychain items are small.
processes.reduce: To stop syncing passwords on this Mac, choose Apple menu › System Settings. Click your name, then iCloud.
processes.summary: Part of macOS. It controls access to keychain items. With iCloud Keychain on, your passwords and other synced items travel between your devices.

processes.block: Blocking it is safe for your internet data, but AirDrop, Handoff and Instant Hotspot discovery may stop working.
breaks: AirDrop can't find devices or send files.
Handoff and Instant Hotspot discovery may stop.
Shared computers in the Finder sidebar may not appear.
processes.name: sharingd
processes.normal: Traffic during an AirDrop transfer is usual. It is about as large as the files you send or receive.
processes.reduce: Open Control Center and click AirDrop. Choose Contacts Only, or turn AirDrop off.
processes.summary: Part of macOS. It runs AirDrop, Handoff, Instant Hotspot discovery and the shared computers in the Finder. AirDrop transfers can show under it.

processes.block: Safe to block for a while, but the app then can't install its updates. Block or pause the app's download instead.
breaks: Downloaded updates of the app can't be installed.
The app may try again each time it starts.
processes.maker: Squirrel.Mac, bundled by each Electron app
processes.name: ShipIt
processes.normal: ShipIt runs for a short time when an app updates. Its own traffic is small or none.
processes.reduce: Open the settings of the app. Turn off automatic updates, if the app has that option.
processes.summary: Part of Squirrel.Mac, the updater that many Electron apps include. It installs an update that the app has already downloaded.

processes.block: Blocking *.signal.org on TCP 443 stops messages. Blocking UDP stops calls and may leave messages working.
breaks: Messages stop when TCP port 443 to the Signal domains is blocked.
Linking Signal Desktop can fail. Signal lists a missing QR code as a sign of a network problem.
Calls fail or end early when UDP is blocked. Group calls need UDP port 10000.
processes.name: Signal
processes.normal: Signal does not publish figures for idle traffic. You should expect small, steady traffic from the open connection.
processes.reduce: Quit Signal Desktop when you are not using it, if you do not need desktop notifications.
processes.summary: The Signal desktop app. It needs *.signal.org on TCP port 443 and UDP, and UDP port 10000 for group calls.

processes.block: Blocking it stops shortcuts syncing between devices and can break shortcuts that use the internet.
breaks: Shortcuts don't sync with your other devices.
Shortcuts with web actions can fail when they run.
Updated malware definitions for shortcuts may not arrive.
processes.name: siriactionsd
processes.normal: Sync traffic is small. Shortcuts are small files.
processes.reduce: Look at the shortcuts that run on a schedule. Open Shortcuts and click Automations.
processes.summary: Part of macOS. It runs and syncs the shortcuts you make in the Shortcuts app, so iCloud sync of shortcuts can show under it.

processes.block: Blocking it can disrupt Siri's understanding of your contacts and apps. Use Siri settings to limit what Siri uses.
breaks: Siri may mis-hear names from your contacts.
Some Siri features may fail.
Subscription tasks for Siri may not complete.
processes.name: siriknowledged
processes.normal: Short bursts are normal. The daemon is mostly idle.
processes.reduce: Choose Apple menu › System Settings › Siri. Apple lists Suggestions and Excluded Apps there.
processes.summary: Part of macOS. Its Mach services are named for Siri entity matching and context. Apple documents Siri data, but not this daemon.

processes.block: Blocking Slack's hosts stops live messages in the app. Block them only on a network where you do not use Slack.
breaks: The app cannot keep its WebSocket connection, so new messages stop arriving.
Sign-in and workspace loading fail when the URLs on Slack's list are blocked.
A proxy that decrypts SSL without WebSocket support breaks the connection.
processes.name: Slack
processes.normal: Slack does not publish figures for idle traffic. You should expect small, steady traffic from the open connection when nobody posts.
processes.reduce: Keep the app current. Old versions can cause connection problems and broken features.
processes.summary: The Slack desktop app. It keeps a persistent WebSocket connection to Slack's messaging servers over port 443, plus HTTPS for everything else.

processes.block: Safe to block if no other computer needs this Mac's files. It's cleaner to turn off File Sharing in Sharing settings.
breaks: Other Macs and PCs can't open this Mac's shared folders.
Backups that other computers make to a shared folder here stop.
heavy: An app working on shared files
processes.name: smbd
processes.normal: With nobody connected, it is quiet.
processes.reduce: Choose Apple menu › System Settings › General › Sharing.
processes.summary: Part of macOS. It is the SMB file server for File Sharing, so its traffic is other computers reading and writing this Mac's shared folders.

processes.block: Don't block it for long. The Mac stops getting macOS and security updates. On a hotspot, turn off automatic downloads instead.
breaks: macOS updates and upgrades can't download or install. Apple's server must sign each update.
Security responses and system data files stop arriving, so security fixes fall behind.
Software Update in System Settings and the softwareupdate command can't check for updates.
processes.name: softwareupdated
processes.normal: Checks are small and short. Large downloads after Apple releases an update are expected.
processes.reduce: Choose Apple menu › System Settings › General › Software Update. Click the Info button next to Automatic Updates.
processes.summary: Part of macOS. It checks for and downloads macOS updates, security responses and system files.

processes.block: Blocking the Sonos app or its ports stops it from finding or controlling speakers. Playback that is already running may continue.
breaks: The app cannot find or control speakers when the control ports are blocked.
Setup fails when UDP 6969 is blocked.
Account sign-in and music services fail when TCP 80 and 443 are blocked.
Spotify Connect and AirPlay to Sonos stop when their ports are blocked.
heavy: A music library on this Mac
processes.name: Sonos
processes.normal: Most of the app's traffic stays on your local network, between the Mac and the speakers.
processes.reduce: Keep the Mac and the speakers on the same network. A guest network may block local traffic.
processes.summary: The Sonos controller app. It finds and controls speakers on your local network, and talks to Sonos servers for content and your account.

processes.block: Safe to block for a while. The app keeps working, but it stops updating. Turn off automatic downloads in the app instead.
breaks: The app can't install its updates, so security fixes wait.
Each app's check for updates fails while it's blocked.
processes.maker: Sparkle project, bundled by each app
processes.name: Autoupdate
processes.normal: Each app that uses Sparkle checks once a day by default. The checks are small.
processes.reduce: Open the app's settings. Many apps that use Sparkle have options to check for and download updates automatically.
processes.summary: Part of Sparkle, an open-source update framework that many Mac apps include. It installs an update after the app downloads it.

processes.block: Safe to block if nobody logs in to this Mac remotely. It's cleaner to turn off Remote Login in Sharing settings.
breaks: SSH, SFTP and scp to this Mac stop working.
Tools that connect to this Mac over SSH, such as remote editors and deploy scripts, fail.
processes.name: sshd
processes.normal: With Remote Login off, macOS's built-in SSH service normally does not listen on port 22. Another service can still use that port.
processes.reduce: Choose Apple menu › System Settings › General › Sharing.
processes.summary: Part of macOS. It is the SSH server for Remote Login, so other computers can log in to this Mac with SSH or copy files with SFTP.

processes.block: Blocking Steam's ports stops sign-in, downloads and online play. Its ports cannot be re-mapped to HTTP.
breaks: You cannot sign in or download games.
Online games that use UDP ports 27000 to 27250 fail to connect.
Remote Play and Steam voice chat stop working.
Proxies and business networks that block its ports break normal operation.
processes.name: Steam
processes.normal: Valve does not publish how much data an idle client uses. Expect small traffic for the store, chat and presence.
processes.reduce: Pause a download in the Steam Downloads page when you need the bandwidth for something else.
processes.summary: The Steam client. Valve lists HTTP and HTTPS for sign-in and downloads, UDP and TCP 27015 to 27050, and UDP 27000 to 27250 for game traffic.

processes.block: Blocking it breaks Classroom on a managed or school Mac. On a personal Mac with no class it is idle.
breaks: Teachers cannot see, lock or control the Mac.
Class content and notices do not arrive.
Classroom may show the Mac as disconnected.
processes.name: studentd
processes.normal: If no class is set up, expect little traffic.
processes.reduce: On a Mac that your school manages, ask your teacher or IT admin. They control the Classroom setup.
processes.summary: Part of macOS. Its man page calls it Classroom's student control agent. It can run with no classes set up.

processes.block: Apple doesn't document what its connections are for. Blocking them may affect suggestions; the settings below turn the features off instead.
breaks: Not documented. Suggestions in Mail, Messages, the keyboard and Siri may get worse or stop.
Found in Apps contacts and events may not appear.
processes.name: suggestd
processes.normal: Its work is processing content, so CPU use is more likely than network traffic.
processes.reduce: Choose Apple menu › System Settings › Siri. Find the suggestion settings for each app.
processes.summary: Part of macOS. It reads content from Mail, Messages and other apps on the Mac to suggest contacts and events. Apple doesn't document much network use.

processes.block: Blocking Surfshark's ports stops the tunnel from connecting. Block them only on a network where you do not use Surfshark.
breaks: The tunnel fails when the port for the chosen protocol is blocked. Another protocol may still connect.
The app stays on the Connecting status or shows an error notification.
With Kill Switch on, a dropped tunnel cuts off your internet connection until you reconnect.
A rule that blocks the app on an antivirus or firewall stops the connection.
processes.name: Surfshark
processes.normal: Surfshark does not publish figures for idle traffic. While connected, the traffic that you route through the tunnel moves through the VPN server.
processes.reduce: If a server fails, try a server in another country.
processes.summary: Surfshark's VPN app. It tunnels your traffic with WireGuard, OpenVPN, IKEv2 or Dausos. Surfshark's blog lists a default port for each protocol.

processes.block: Apple doesn't document what depends on it. Blocking it saves little data and may affect features that Apple doesn't name.
breaks: Not documented. Apple doesn't say which features use the Symptom Framework.
Because it runs as the networking user and reacts to network changes, network features may be affected.
processes.name: symptomsd
processes.normal: It is part of macOS and usually shows little or no traffic of its own.
processes.reduce: There is no user setting for symptomsd.
processes.summary: Part of macOS, barely documented. Apple says only that it provides services for the Symptom Framework. It runs as the networking user and reacts to network changes.

processes.block: Don't block it. Gatekeeper's online checks protect the Mac against known malware and revoked apps.
breaks: Gatekeeper can't check new apps online for known malware or revoked developer certificates.
Revocation tickets for malicious apps may not reach this Mac.
Opening a new app can take longer while the check waits for the network.
processes.name: syspolicyd
processes.normal: Short connections when you open new or updated apps are usual. They are small.
processes.reduce: There is no setting to reduce these checks safely. They are small.
processes.summary: Part of macOS. It runs the system policy that includes Gatekeeper, which checks new and changed apps for known malware and revoked certificates.

processes.block: Blocking Tailscale's hosts stops sign-in and device discovery, and the tunnel may drop. Block it only if you do not use it.
breaks: The client cannot reach the coordination server, so it cannot update the list of your devices.
Direct device traffic needs UDP, and blocking it forces relays or breaks connections.
Blocking TCP 443 to DERP relays removes the fallback path.
Remote access to this Mac over your tailnet stops.
processes.name: Tailscale
processes.normal: With no traffic between your devices, Tailscale's traffic should be small. Expect short exchanges with the coordination servers.
processes.reduce: To pause the tunnel, click the Tailscale icon in the menu bar and turn Tailscale off.
processes.summary: Tailscale's VPN client. It talks to Tailscale's coordination servers over HTTPS, relays over TCP 443, and sends WireGuard traffic to your other devices over UDP.

processes.block: Blocking Telegram's ports stops messages, but the app may retry on other ports. Block it only on a network where you do not use it.
breaks: Messages and updates stop when the main connection to your data centre is blocked.
Photos, video and files fail to load when media data centres are blocked.
Sign-in fails when the client cannot reach any data centre.
processes.name: Telegram
processes.normal: Telegram does not publish figures for idle traffic. You should expect small, steady traffic from the open connection when nobody writes.
processes.reduce: Leave channels that you do not read. Large public channels load media from CDN nodes.
processes.summary: The Telegram desktop app. Telegram documents TCP connections on ports 80, 443 and 5222 to regional data centres, plus separate connections for media.

processes.block: Don't block it. A wrong clock makes valid certificates look expired, so secure websites and apps fail.
breaks: The clock drifts. Secure websites can then show certificate errors, such as ERR_CERT_DATE_INVALID.
Sign-ins and other features that check the time may fail.
Apple doesn't list a fallback for macOS without NTP.
processes.name: timed
processes.normal: The requests are tiny. A time request and its answer are a few small packets.
processes.reduce: There is nothing to reduce. Keep it on. See “This Connection Is Not Private” and certificate warnings on a Mac.
processes.summary: Part of macOS. It keeps the clock correct with NTP, so it sends small requests to a time server such as time.apple.com.

processes.block: Don't block it. This can interfere with certificate trust checks, and Apple services that need validation can fail.
breaks: Some certificate revocation checks may fail or rely on cached results, depending on the service and its trust policy.
Apple says that its devices must reach the certificate validation hosts to validate the certificates of its own services.
On a company network, a proxy that blocks these checks causes certificate errors. See Corporate proxy certificates break Terminal tools on a Mac.
heavy: A first visit to many sites
processes.name: trustd
processes.normal: Small, short connections are usual, mostly when you visit many secure sites or open apps.
processes.reduce: Trust policies and revocation behavior depend on the certificate and the service using it.
processes.summary: Part of macOS. It checks certificates for every app, and asks certificate authorities whether a certificate was revoked. Its connections are small.

processes.block: Blocking VS Code's hosts stops updates, the marketplace and Settings Sync. The editor still opens local files.
breaks: The editor cannot update itself.
You cannot search for or install extensions.
Settings Sync stops.
Extensions that need their own servers, such as remote development, stop working.
processes.name: Code Helper
processes.normal: Small requests at start-up and when you open the extensions view are usual.
processes.reduce: Review the hosts in Microsoft's list. Decide which of them your network policy should allow.
processes.summary: Visual Studio Code and its helper processes. They contact Microsoft's update, extension marketplace and sync servers, and whatever your extensions and terminals reach.

processes.block: Blocking UDP makes media fall back to TCP or TLS. Blocking port 443 to Webex's domains stops sign-in and meetings.
breaks: Signalling fails when port 443 to the Webex domains is blocked, so you cannot sign in or join.
Media quality can drop when UDP is blocked and the app falls back to TCP or TLS.
Calls fail when UDP, TCP and TLS media paths are all blocked.
processes.name: Webex
processes.normal: Cisco does not publish figures for idle traffic in this article. You should expect small traffic for signalling when you are not in a meeting.
processes.reduce: Leave meetings when they end. Media then stops.
processes.summary: The Webex desktop app. Cisco documents HTTPS signalling on port 443 and SRTP media over UDP on ports 5004 and 9000, with TCP and TLS as fallbacks.

processes.block: Don't block it. Safari and every app that shows web pages stop loading. Block the website instead.
breaks: Safari can't load any page.
Apps that show web content through WebKit, such as Mail's remote content, stop loading it.
A rule on this process acts on all browsing. Block the host instead, for every app or one app.
processes.name: com.apple.WebKit.Networking
processes.normal: A lot of traffic is normal while you browse. It is the sites you visit.
processes.reduce: Close tabs that play video or refresh in the background.
processes.summary: Part of macOS. It is WebKit's network process, which does all network access for Safari and for apps that show web pages, so their browsing shows under it.

processes.block: You can't block it with a firewall, because it isn't internet traffic. To stop its link for a while, turn off AirDrop; Kilobat can pause it for you.
breaks: AirDrop can't find or send to nearby devices.
Other features that use the peer-to-peer link between nearby devices may stop.
processes.name: wifip2pd
processes.normal: wifip2pd itself moves little data. The bytes of a transfer belong to the feature that uses the link: AirDrop is under sharingd.
processes.reduce: Open Control Center and click AirDrop. Turn AirDrop off while you are on a call or playing.
processes.summary: Part of macOS. It manages peer-to-peer Wi-Fi, the direct link that AirDrop and other nearby-device features use.

processes.block: Do not block it. Your Mac loses protection against known malware and revoked apps.
breaks: XProtect signatures stop updating, so new malware is not recognised.
Remediation of known infections may not run.
Revocation and notarisation data may go stale.
processes.name: xprotectd
processes.normal: Small checks about once a day are the expected pattern.
processes.reduce: No action is needed. Updates are small and daily.
processes.summary: Part of macOS. It is a subsystem of XProtect, which detects and blocks known malware. Signature updates are checked daily.

processes.block: Blocking it stops Zoom meetings on this Mac. To save data, turn off video in meetings instead.
breaks: You can't join or host Zoom meetings in the desktop app.
Zoom Chat and other Zoom features in the app stop.
Updates to the app can't download.
processes.name: zoom.us
processes.normal: A lot of traffic during a meeting is normal. Video uses far more than audio.
processes.reduce: Turn off your camera when you don't need it. Video uses most of the data.
processes.summary: The Zoom desktop app. During meetings it sends and receives audio and video; Zoom also updates itself if automatic updates are on.
